correctness.rationale: On the associated superdiagonal filtration, a bracket with X advances by at least one diagonal. In n−2 brackets only the nearest diagonal of X can contribute, only first-superdiagonal input matters, and the only surviving target is E_{1n}. From E_{i,i+1} the elementary bracket steps extend the interval left with coefficient a_{i−1} or right with coefficient −a_{i+1}; iterating requires i−1 left and n−i−1 right extensions. Every ordering has the same signed product of all a_j except a_i, so the path multiplicity is the displayed binomial coefficient. This proves the formula and the rank-zero/one Jordan-block criterion even in characteristic two. The two disjoint support cases give the claimed count (and dividing by q^d gives the probability). For the scheme, a monomial belongs to the intersection of (a_j) for j outside I and (a_i,a_k) for pairs in I exactly when it includes every outside variable and all but at most one inside variable. This gives precisely the ideal generated by the top-power entries and proves reducedness, not just agreement on finite-field points. Both endpoint binomials are units, including for n=3. Lucas gives the digit product and says every binomial survives iff the digits of n−2 below the leading digit are all p−1, equivalently n−1=c p^r in the prescribed range. This is an all-n algebraic check. The frozen finite checks and output were inspected, not rerun or used to infer the theorem.

value.rationale: The longest Jordan chain of the adjoint action is a natural conjugacy invariant. The result specifies exactly how it degenerates scheme-theoretically and how often it occurs across fields, and gives a characteristic-sensitive, nonconstant codimension law across dimensions. That all-dimensional information is usable without claiming any new n=5 census or classifying the remaining Jordan partition.
